craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra as power-filled state (FIRST vīra in the work — color shift from śānta supplication to heroic testimony). Sanskrit-first: antaka (ENDer — death named to its face, kept); asmi (I AM — the ground is a state, not a plea); ghora-bhairava-tejas (dread-power, kept dread). Rows: 7 (‘O Ender’ opens — address before petition; death faced first), 1 (‘dread Bhairava-power’ closes — the state named last), 5 (prayer tread: plea L1, ground L2). Close: ‘filled with dread Bhairava-power’. Rupture: L2 (prayer turns to testimony — begging turns to possessing; argmap: power declared, not begged). Rejected: ‘awesome’ — killed: ghora is dread, awe admires; ‘fierce gaze’ — killed: raudra + bhīṣaṇa both present, both kept; ‘avert’ for ‘turn from me’ — killed: parāṅmukha kept bodily (turned-face). Read aloud: O-END-er — TURN-from-me THIS most-WRATH-ful AND-terr-i-BLE-gaze … STEAD-fast in ŚAṄ-ka-ra's SER-vice … i-AM-filled WITH-dread BHAI-ra-va-POW-er.

lines: O Ender — turn from me this most wrathful and terrible gaze.
Steadfast in Śaṅkara’s service and contemplation, I am filled with dread Bhairava-power.
l4.sanskrit_cite: antaka māṃ prati mā dṛśam enāṃ krodhakarālatamāṃ vinidhehi śaṅkarasevanacintanadhīro bhīṣaṇabhairavaśaktimayo 'smi

reads_against.argmap: How does the devotee turn aside death's gaze? → Prayer first, then the ground: power declared as state, not begged. The devotee testifies to possessing power, grounded in service and contemplation.
c1_essence: Death's gaze is turned aside by prayer: O Ender, do not direct this wrathful-terrible gaze toward me.
The ground of the prayer: firm in Śaṅkara-service and contemplation, filled with terrifying Bhairava-power — asmi (I am).
Power first invoked against death's gaze, then declared as state. Śaṅkara here is Śiva, not Śaṅkarācārya.
